hook: Telangana spent *17%* less than it budgeted, says PRS
hook_b: Telangana spent *17%* less than it budgeted, says PRS
tldr: PRS Legislative Research's State of Finances Report 2026-27 says Telangana's actual spending fell 17% short of its budget, against a 9% average across states. Revenue expenditure was 20% below budget, and revenue receipts were 23% below projections between 2021-22 and 2024-25.

beats.what: A PRS report finds Telangana's spending fell well short of its budgets.
beats.why: Revenue receipts came in 23% below projections, among the largest gaps in India.
beats.care: Budget promises on welfare and services may not match what is actually spent.

effects.label: Less room as borrowing is restricted

cards.title: 🆕 What's new
cards.body: Siasat (Nov 20): only Manipur (39%) and Jammu and Kashmir (32%) had bigger revenue receipt shortfalls than Telangana.

cards.q: Should states publish how much of each budget promise was actually spent?

qs: Which schemes took the biggest cuts when receipts fell short?
Does budgeting closer to real income change what gets promised?

facts.t: Telangana's capital outlay was only *2%* below budget, against a 17% average shortfall across states.
Only Manipur (*39%*) and J&K (32%) missed revenue receipt targets by more than Telangana.

viz.verdict: A bigger gap means less of the budget reached people
Income fell far short of what budgets assumed

learn.t: Revenue expenditure = recurring costs like salaries, pensions, interest and subsidies

watch: How the 2027-28 Telangana budget projects receipts after this gap.

sources.name: Siasat
sources.title: Telangana falls short of budget spending by 17 pc: PRS report

fact: Telangana spent *17%* less than it budgeted, almost twice the 9% state average
twist: Capital outlay on roads, bridges and irrigation was only 2% short; the big gap was salaries, subsidies and routine costs.
